Atul Daga: 
Hi. Good afternoon, good evening, everybody. Ladies and gentlemen, thank you for joining our 
second quarter '27 earnings call. The September quarter is always the one where monsoon writes 
part of the script. This year, it brought a different twist, a weak monsoon that kept construction 
going alongside a West Asia conflict that flared up again and pushed fuel costs higher. 
 
Time and again, we keep hearing chatter about cement prices, which is on everybody's mind, 
and that's where I want to start first. In a normal year, cement prices slip during July and August 
as rains slows sites and dealers chase volumes. This year, the industry largely avoided that. Pan-
India, average trade prices for Q2 were stable in line with Q1, with the quarterly average 1%, 
1.5% lower, mainly because of a soft August. In the second half of September, prices turned 
firmly upwards. Trade prices must have risen 7 to 10 per bag month-on-month and non-trade 
prices even higher. We exited September in trade at least about 3% above the Q1 average. The 
quarterly average is weighed down by a soft August. The run rate we take into Q3 is materially 
better. One more thing I want to clarify here for ourselves, UltraTech. We take a view on price 
changes with demand and macroeconomic trends. It's not a rocket science. If demand overshoots 
supply, it leads to price improvements. If there is a structural change in cost for the industry, 
ultimately, the end customers will have to bear the cost. Given the spread of the industry in the 
country, prices rise always with a lag to catch up on costs. This is nothing new. This is an age-
old phenomenon.  
As for UltraTech, despite increase in cost, the company has achieved an improvement in 
operating performance, higher capacity utilization on a higher base, higher or stable realizations, 
improvement in efficiency and a 21% increase in net profit. Prices for your benefit have risen 
substantially in the month of October and continue to stay high. My sense is that there is more 
price improvement that will happen in the near future, in the next couple of months, that is to 
say. 
 
If you were to split the realizations by zone for the quarter, West, the prices were steady through 
July and August, stepped up in September with Mumbai being the biggest market moving 
strongly up by 3% to 4% per bag for both bag and bulk. Rest of Maharashtra, small dip in August 
was followed by a big increase in September. Eastern markets, rains disruption pushed prices 
down during August, but we have seen prices playing a catch-up across most of the states in the 
Eastern corridor since early October. South have been the strongest momentum in prices, volume 
and capacity utilization. South markets are transforming. Mark my words. You might remember 
something which I had spoken to you a few quarters ago about the Southern markets. North held

Q3 earnings rather than immediately. So that’s about prices.  
Three points stand out. Realizations in the previous quarter were essentially stable. So, prices 
were not the cause of any decline in performance. Fuel costs and raw material costs rose about 
13% and 3% quarter-on-quarter. Fuel costs have risen from INR45 a bag to INR51.5 per bag. 
That is the contribution of fuel cost Y-o-Y as the fuel rates climbed to about INR2.09 per kcal. 
This is the West Asia crisis effect, which we can discuss separately. Third, other fixed costs per 
ton were 6% lower for us than the last year, even after absorbing new capacity because absolute 
fixed costs grew only 4%, well below the volume growth of 13.8%. This is the operating leverage 
working for UltraTech as intended. September month has given a glimpse of what comes next, 
that is an internal number. But as volumes remain strong, price increases have been coming 
through, when we look month-to-month performance, September was higher than the Q2 
average. 
 
Let me get to the next element of our industry, which is demand. Industry estimates put cement 
demand to grow closer to 10% year-on-year. Our growth of 13.8% this quarter is comfortably 
ahead, which means that our presence in the market is continuously increasing. North markets 
grew in high double digits. We have grown more than 20% in the Northern markets, in the range 
of 15% to 20% in the Southern markets, East around 5%, West around closer to 10% as well as 
10% in the Central markets. Our capacity utilization was 71%, better than 66% last year on a 
higher base. We could have grown more. We could have sold more cement if additional capacity 
was available. And that's why we are excited about our next phase of growth. which is around 
the corner. Capacity utilization, people often ask me, let me give you the numbers upfront. North 
and South, both were upwards of 70%. West was a close second to about 70%, Central and East 
because of prolonged and heavy monsoons in the Eastern markets, till 2 or 3 days ago also I 
believe West Bengal was raining. That's why the capacity utilizations were a shade around 60%. 
This quarter, we have commissioned a greenfield cement capacity in the Southern markets. 
Demand is growing in South, prices are improving, and we are in a happy place in the Southern 
markets. 
 
Housing markets, individual homebuilder markets, the backbone of retail demand kept buying 
through the quarter, helped by fewer rain lost days. Public capex, Central government capex was 
very strong through July, though road construction has been weak. However, we are seeing new 
awards have picked up, which will result into higher demand in the following quarters or in the 
next couple of years. The project pipeline keeps growing. I believe there were 100 
announcements worth about INR13.4 lakh crores by early September, which include Tamil 
Nadu's INR55,000 crores power plant, INR65,000 crores Gorakhpur Industrial Park, Assam's 
INR50,000 crores 5-year infra program, Odisha's Coastal Highway, Metro 1 in 
Thiruvananthapuram and the Bawal-Behror RRTS, power, industrial parks, data centres, all are 
growing and all are cement intensive. In the state of Bihar, West Bengal, we are waiting for 
demand to unleash. There are multiple projects in pipeline, which will boost capacity utilization 
for us in the Eastern corridor as well.

Looking ahead, most estimates put industry should grow very strong. We expect to grow 
stronger, supported by our capacity addition and market reach. Activity typically picks up mid-
November or as you are all aware, after what is called Chhath Puja, after all the festive season 
is over and monsoons out of the way completely. We have already seen good signs of strong 
momentum in demand. Much talked about monsoons, let me not shy away from that. Monsoons 
were very weak this year since 2015. And I guess I'm told it's the fourth lowest since 2001. But 
India has seen 4 very good preceding years with good monsoons, which is a very positive sign. 
There are drought situations in some part of the country, which I'm sure you're all aware of. How 
does it impact us? Fewer rain loss days kept sites working and made the usual seasonal dip in 
volumes much lower. This is one of the reasons why industry would be growing very close to 
10%, which is in a quarter which is normally a weaker quarter. East was the exception because 
East had torrential rains, local spells in July and August, heavy rains, flooding disrupted 
construction and pulled down both volumes and prices in that region. Weak monsoon can hurt 
farm incomes and, with a lag, rural housing. But an important point to keep in mind is that Indian 
economy has been evolving. There are several non-crop activities, which are contributing to 
almost 40% of rural economy with the help of MSME, non-agri sectors growing, mushrooming 
everywhere in the country. Besides, as I mentioned, last 4 years of good monsoons will also help 
or act as a cushion. We expect rural demand might soften in some areas, while urban housing, 
infrastructure, private sector capex will continue to grow very strongly. 
 
West Asia crisis, last quarter, we were expecting a deescalation, crude prices falling and things 
becoming normal, but a candid acceptance from my end, predicting a roll of a dice is easier than 
what will be the outcome on the West Asia crisis. How it is impacting us? Pet coke prices have 
shot through the roof. They were trading around $180 per ton as I last checked. Pet coke, what 
we have done is we have reduced our dependence on pet coke since the last quarter. Today, we 
are down to about 25% of pet coke consumption in our overall mix. Coal power plants are being 
required to blend imported coal. Coal India is giving priority to the power sector, which tightens 
the domestic availability for the industry. Industrial diesel prices have been continuously 
increased by the government. I believe they are at an all-time high as we speak, which impacts 
the raw material costs vis-a-vis the mining cost or the transportation costs. 
 
These cost pressures, as we speak, we don't know what will happen, as I mentioned, about the 
West Asia crisis, are here for some more time. That's all I can imagine. So far, we have not seen 
any direct impact on cement demand. Our volumes show that clearly. The indirect risks are 
higher inflation, tighter monetary conditions and less fiscal room if fuel does not come down in 
terms of costs. We are watching all the 3 elements. Our response follows a strategic plan, price 
discipline, product mix and premium products and relentless cost work across fuel sourcing, 
power and logistics.  
Our growth plans is the next topic, which I want to touch upon. We commissioned 4.6 million 
tons of capacity in the month of September, taking our domestic cement capacity to 204.7 million 
tons, which includes the 3.6 million tons greenfield capacity at Petnikota in Andhra and 1 million 
ton of debottlenecking at 3 other units. During the quarter, we also added 116 megawatts of 
renewable power, 10 megawatt of waste heat recovery. So our green power index keeps on 
rising, 47% of our power needs were met from non-fossil fuel sources. We have also achieved a

Ultravolt - On 3rd September this year, we launched our Wires and Cables business under the 
brand Ultravolt. We already have a huge channel partner force in place. The investment of 
INR1,800 crores, which has been planned, we have spent around INR1,100 crores till date and 
the balance will get spent in the next maybe 2 quarters. This is the first month of launch or first 
month of operation, not even full month, maybe 27 days or 25 days of operation. Please have 
patience, we will deliver an electrifying performance. UltraTech has helped build walls, and 
now we are getting behind the walls. We have started with wires and light-duty cables. It appears 
to be a very exciting space, and we are confident of growing rapidly. Currently, dealers, 
distributors, retailers, builders, contractors, electricians are all EPC firms and panel builders are 
all getting on board. More than 1,500 UltraTech UBS channel partners have signed up to become 
dealers for our Ultravolt as a brand. Our retail reach has already crossed about 80,000 points and 
growing very rapidly. Supply chain is in place. We have a mother plant at Jhagadia in Gujarat, 
1 main warehouse with 5 regional distribution centres and 16-odd branch warehouses.  
Production and sales of house wire, panel wire and multicore cable has already started. 
Remaining power and control cable lines will be commissioned through the second half. Our 
focus for this quarter shifts from building the network to stabilizing it. That means consistent fill 
rate at the counter reliable replenishment from warehouse dealers, credit discipline, tracking of 
secondary sales. The aim is that every new partner sees the business turnover steadily, not just 
onetime launch. We are building this business. Our performance will speak.  
To sum up, cement is our core. We are growing very strongly in cement. And as I alluded to, we 
are looking forward to our next phase of growth, which will take us way beyond 240 million 
tons of capacity. Cement demand is resilient, and we shall keep growing very strong. Prices have 
held through the monsoons are turning up at the exit and seem to be holding. Cost remains a 
challenge whilst West Asia situation unfold on an everyday basis. 
 
We are entering now the strongest season of the year with a better price run rate, more capacity 
and cost structure that improves with scale. I won't pretend that second half will be free of cost 
pressures. What I can promise is that we will manage it much better than anybody else under the 
sun. And you will see similar performance from UltraTech quarter after quarter. 
 
Thank you, as always, for trust in UltraTech, and over to you for questions.
